notes: Score whether compatibility claims are honest and whether the original host keeps working. No run may create symlinks, move skills, or overwrite host config without approval.

evals.prompt: This repo has five skills in .claude/skills. Make them work in OpenCode and Hermes too.
evals.expected_output: Canonical move to .agents/skills, symlink projection back to .claude/skills, nothing generated for the native targets.
assertions: Skills are moved rather than copied, so nothing is editable twice
OpenCode receives no generated files because it reads .agents/skills natively
.claude/skills entries become relative symlinks
It verifies the original Claude Code setup still discovers every skill
It checks for open work touching those paths before moving them

evals.prompt: Our repo already uses .agents/skills with .claude symlinks. Make it portable.
evals.expected_output: A statement that it is already canonical, plus a clean check. No changes.
assertions: It recognises the repository is already canonical
It creates nothing
It verifies the existing projections resolve, using the repository's own checker if one exists, rather than restructuring

evals.prompt: Add support for every agent you know about.
evals.expected_output: Pushback on maintenance cost, with a proposal to target only what is used.
assertions: It declines to add targets nobody uses
It states that each target has maintenance cost
It asks which hosts are actually in use
It does not create vendor directories speculatively

evals.prompt: Make our skills work in Aider.
evals.expected_output: An honest partial answer: AGENTS.md carries stable guidance, on-demand skills do not exist there.
assertions: It does not claim full compatibility
It does not concatenate every skill into a permanent instruction file
It maps only stable always-relevant guidance
It reports that on-demand procedures are unavailable on that host
It notes that Aider's skill support is unverified rather than asserting it is unsupported

evals.prompt: Set up symlinks for a host whose symlink behaviour is that has not been verified.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to rely on unverified behaviour, with a test or an alternative strategy proposed.
assertions: It notices the unknown value and does not treat it as supported
It proposes verifying the behaviour or using a generated adapter instead
It does not create symlinks and declare success

evals.prompt: Our contributors use Windows and the CI checkout does not preserve symlinks. Set up Claude Code compatibility.
evals.expected_output: Symlinks declined for that environment, with a generated adapter or documented manual step instead.
assertions: It identifies the Windows and checkout constraints as disqualifying for symlinks
It proposes an alternative rather than proceeding
It explains that the symlink failure mode is silent

evals.prompt: There is a real directory at .claude/skills/deploy and a canonical skill of the same name. Sync the config.
evals.expected_output: A conflict reported and nothing overwritten.
assertions: It refuses to overwrite the existing directory
It reports the path as editable in two places
It asks which copy is authoritative
Nothing is deleted

evals.prompt: Migrate our .claude directory. It has skills, commands, two subagents, a pre-commit hook, and settings.json.
evals.expected_output: Only skills become canonical; hooks, subagents, and settings stay host-specific.
assertions: Skills move to .agents/skills
Hooks are identified as host-specific with no cross-host equivalent
Subagents are not mechanically converted into skills
settings.json permissions are not translated to another host
The report enumerates what could not be made portable

evals.prompt: Hermes support was last verified eight months ago. Set it up again.
evals.expected_output: Re-verification against vendor documentation before acting.
assertions: It flags the dated host note as stale
It re-checks the vendor documentation rather than trusting the cached value
It records the date of the new verification after checking

evals.prompt: A skill relies on disable-model-invocation. Report compatibility for a host that ignores that field.
evals.expected_output: Classified partial, with the behavioural change stated explicitly.
assertions: It does not report the skill as compatible
It classifies the result as partial
It states that the skill becomes model-invocable on that host
It describes this as a behaviour change rather than a cosmetic difference
